topic: B2B Paid Search and Rising Ad Costs
headline: Same B2B Google Ads Keywords Cost About 21% More, Agency Data Shows via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
keyNotes: Surprisingly, the cost for businesses to advertise on Google using specific search terms (called "keywords") has gone up significantly. A study found that for 14 business-to-business (B2B) companies, the cost they pay each time someone clicks their ad (called "cost-per-click" or CPC) increased by about 21% for the same keywords compared to last year.

One big reason for these rising ad costs is simply spending more money. The study showed that for every 10% more a company spent on their ad campaigns, their cost-per-click went up by about 1.4% on top of the general market increase.

Some companies saw much larger increases; for instance, one advertiser who nearly quadrupled their ad spending saw their cost-per-click for the same keywords jump by a massive 132%. This suggests that automated systems that bid for ads might be pushing costs higher by entering more expensive ad slots.

While the overall market generally pushed ad costs up, individual company choices also played a role. For some advertisers, 22 percentage points of their average 36% cost-per-click increase were due to the market, but another 3 percentage points were because they increased their own spending.

It's crucial to remember that paying more for ads doesn't automatically mean better results. The study didn't look at whether these companies actually got more sales or leads for their higher ad spending, so we don't know if the increased cost was worth it.
question: The study found that while ad costs went up by as much as 132% for some, it didn't track whether these higher costs actually led to more sales or customers for the businesses. If you were managing a budget for your own business, how would you decide if paying significantly more for something (like advertising or any other business expense) was actually a good investment, especially if you couldn't directly see the return?
